subproblem.title: Good radius: a level in (ρ, ρ') with a prescribed a.e. property, a μ-null sphere and a Markov bound
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on (the Borel sets of) ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P, and ρ < ρ' real numbers. Let g : ℝ → [0, ∞] be L¹-a.e. measurable (L¹ = Lebesgue measure on ℝ), let I ∈ [0, ∞] with ∫_ℝ g dL¹ ≤ I (lower Lebesgue integral), and let p be a property of real numbers holding for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Assume μ(B̄_{ρ'}(y)) < ∞. Then there is t ∈ ℝ with ρ < t < ρ' such that p(t) holds, μ(∂B_t(y)) = 0, where ∂B_t(y) = {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x − y| = t} (Metric.sphere y t), and g(t) ≤ (2/(ρ' − ρ))·I, the product being computed in [0, ∞] as ENNReal.ofReal(2/(ρ' − ρ))·I.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (ρ ρ' : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (I : ℝ≥0∞) (p : ℝ → Prop), ρ < ρ' → μ (closedBall y ρ') ≠ ∞ → AEMeasurable g → ∫⁻ t, g t ≤ I → (∀ᵐ t, p t) → ∃ t : ℝ, ρ < t ∧ t < ρ' ∧ p t ∧ μ (sphere y t) = 0 ∧ g t ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 / (ρ' - ρ)) * I
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (choice of t), which follows Simon 7.2.4, displays (3)–(5) (chapter-07.txt lines 193–204: the level α is chosen by the slicing theory so that the slice is good and M(T_j⌞∂W_α) = 0), with the factor-2 averaging selection of Simon Ch. 2, 6.7(1) (chapter-02.txt lines 1512–1530). The parent's three sets E₁ (slice property), E₂ (null spheres) and E₃ (Markov bound) are abstracted here into p, μ and (g, I). Notation: J := (ρ, ρ'), δ := ρ' − ρ > 0, c := ofReal(2/δ) ∈ [0, ∞]; L¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, used as an outer measure (monotone and countably subadditive on arbitrary subsets of ℝ); ∂B_s := ∂B_s(y) = {x : |x − y| = s}, B̄_s := B̄_s(y).
1. Facts about c. Since 2/δ > 0 we have c ≠ 0, and c ≠ ∞ because ofReal is finite. Moreover c⁻¹ = ofReal((2/δ)⁻¹) = ofReal(δ/2) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos and (2/δ)⁻¹ = δ/2).
2. The exceptional set of p. Let N₁ := {t ∈ ℝ : p(t) fails}. Since p holds L¹-a.e., L¹(N₁) = 0 (ae_iff).
3. Charged spheres. Let ν := μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}, i.e. ν(A) = μ(A ∩ B̄_{ρ'}) for Borel A. Then ν(ℝ^P) = μ(B̄_{ρ'}) < ∞, so ν is a finite (hence s-finite) measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). The spheres ∂B_s, s ∈ ℝ, are closed, hence Borel, and pairwise disjoint: if x ∈ ∂B_s ∩ ∂B_{s'} then s = |x − y| = s'. For an s-finite measure only countably many members of a pairwise disjoint family of measurable sets have positive measure (Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion). Hence N₂ := {s ∈ ℝ : 0 < ν(∂B_s)} is countable, and L¹(N₂) = 0 because L¹ has no atoms (Set.Countable.measure_zero). Moreover, if s ≤ ρ' then ∂B_s ⊆ B̄_s ⊆ B̄_{ρ'}, so ν(∂B_s) = μ(∂B_s ∩ B̄_{ρ'}) = μ(∂B_s) (Measure.restrict_apply for the closed set ∂B_s).
4. The Markov set. Let N₃ := {t ∈ ℝ : c·I < g(t)}. We show L¹(N₃) ≤ ofReal(δ/2) by cases on I.
 (a) I = 0. Then ∫ g dL¹ ≤ 0, so ∫ g dL¹ = 0, and since g is a.e.-measurable, g = 0 L¹-a.e. (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'). As c·I = 0, every t ∈ N₃ has g(t) > 0, so N₃ ⊆ {t : g(t) ≠ 0}, an L¹-null set; hence L¹(N₃) = 0 ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
 (b) I = ∞. Since c ≠ 0, c·I = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top), and no t satisfies ∞ < g(t). So N₃ = ∅ and L¹(N₃) = 0 ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
 (c) I ≠ 0 and I ≠ ∞. Put ε := c·I; then ε ≠ 0 (as c ≠ 0 and I ≠ 0) and ε ≠ ∞ (as c ≠ ∞ and I ≠ ∞). Since N₃ ⊆ {t : ε ≤ g(t)}, Markov's inequality for the a.e.-measurable g (meas_ge_le_lintegral_div) gives L¹(N₃) ≤ L¹({ε ≤ g}) ≤ (∫ g dL¹)/ε ≤ I/(c·I). Finally I/(c·I) = (c·I)⁻¹·I = c⁻¹·(I⁻¹·I) = c⁻¹ (ENNReal.mul_inv, using c ≠ 0 and c ≠ ∞, and I⁻¹·I = 1 since I ≠ 0, ∞), and c⁻¹ = ofReal(δ/2) by step 1. Hence L¹(N₃) ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
5. Covering. Suppose, for a contradiction, that no t satisfies ρ < t < ρ', p(t), μ(∂B_t) = 0 and g(t) ≤ c·I. Then J ⊆ N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃: otherwise take t ∈ J outside N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃. Then p(t) holds (t ∉ N₁); ν(∂B_t) = 0 (t ∉ N₂), hence μ(∂B_t) = ν(∂B_t) = 0 by step 3 because t < ρ'; and g(t) ≤ c·I (t ∉ N₃). So t has all four properties, contradicting the assumption.
6. By monotonicity and subadditivity of L¹ and steps 2–4, ofReal(δ) = L¹(J) ≤ L¹(N₁) + L¹(N₂) + L¹(N₃) ≤ 0 + 0 + ofReal(δ/2) = ofReal(δ/2) (Real.volume_Ioo). Since δ/2 ≥ 0, this gives δ ≤ δ/2 (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff), i.e. δ ≤ 0, contradicting δ > 0.
7. Hence there is t with ρ < t < ρ', p(t), μ(∂B_t(y)) = 0 and g(t) ≤ ofReal(2/(ρ' − ρ))·I. ∎
proof_key_steps: N₁ := {t : ¬p(t)} is L¹-null; N₂ := {s : μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}(y)(∂B_s(y)) > 0} is countable (pairwise disjoint closed spheres, finite measure), hence L¹-null; μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}(y) and μ agree on ∂B_s(y) for s ≤ ρ'.
N₃ := {t : (2/(ρ'−ρ))·I < g(t)} has L¹-measure ≤ (ρ'−ρ)/2: if I = 0 then g = 0 a.e.; if I = ∞ then N₃ = ∅; otherwise Markov's inequality with ε = (2/(ρ'−ρ))·I.
If no good t existed, (ρ, ρ') ⊆ N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃, so ρ' − ρ ≤ 0 + 0 + (ρ' − ρ)/2, a contradiction.

audit.reason: The prose includes every hypothesis and matches the standalone Lean proposition. Restricting μ to the finite closed ball makes charged spheres countable. The proof correctly treats I = 0, I = ∞ and finite positive I separately, then combines the Markov estimate with the two null exceptional sets. The covering contradiction proves the exact conclusion without circularity. The frozen slicing contract supplies the required global integral bound in the parent assembly.
